title: Greta Gris
source_notes: Expanded from six identical two-bar hooks to a complete main-theme A/B and a distinct closing tag. A and B pitches, rhythms and tonic-ending difference were read from the complete four-bar Conrad Chords notation. The tag is the top voice of bars14–15 in the public licensed Musicnotes Christina Petrando preview MN0201958: C5(2), D5(1), G4(1) | G4(.5), B4(.5), D5(.5), F5(.5), C5(2). Conrad C-major melody is transposed down5 semitones; the octave-higher Musicnotes tag is transposed down17 semitones, both into the previously accepted G-major D3–D4 register. Existing144 BPM and playful style are retained. The arrangement form A–B–tag–B / A–B–tag–B and all bass/chord/fart responses are creative arrangement choices, not a claim to reproduce the complete television opening or ending recording. No original recording or vocal asset is used.
musical_direction: A complete little cartoon performance with three distinct melodic phrases instead of one tiny loop. Play A–B–tag–B, then reprise with the recorded fart voices and band response varied; keep the lead low and clear. The B phrases resolve on a held G3 and the tag starts on its longer G3–A3 answer. Use the existing playful springy root/fifth bass, duck-like chord replies and quiet offbeat ticks. Reserve little splutters for phrase gaps, do not cover the four ascending eighth notes, and let the final two-beat G3 cadence resolve without another hook restart.

musical_direction: Heavy half-time rock march at the accepted 68 BPM. Keep all 27 lead events and the F3-Eb4 register; do not smooth over the four 0.125-beat grace figures at beat 18. Under the lead, use low rounded root-and-fifth farts, restrained alternating eighth-note gallops, dry thudding downbeats and rasping backbeats. Add smaller nasal chord replies at phrase ends and quiet rattling fills into beats 8, 12 and 18. Build the second half with more timbres and wider backing, while leaving the melodic wet attacks clearly above the ensemble. Land the final G3 with a low G-minor fart ensemble.

musical_direction: Dance arrangement at the accepted 126 BPM. Preserve all 72 syncopated lead notes, their low G#2-B3 register, and the three identical 16-beat chorus loops. Support the recognizable hook with a firm four-on-the-floor deep fart kick, short backbeat splats, quiet offbeat squeaks and springy root/fifth bass. Use sparse upstroke-style chord farts to answer the 0.75-beat lead, and keep the 0.5-beat run at each loop end clear. First loop lean, second loop with wider chord puffs, third loop with little splutter fills and a fuller bass. Do not octave-shift any melody note or add a competing tune.

title: Sommartider
key: A major; low vocal lead A2-F#3
source_notes: Replaces the former 10-note opening repeated six times with a compact, complete two-half VOCAL REFRAIN, read from arranger TheddyKeys' own public Sommartider piano tutorial, chapter Refrang 0:44-1:13. The high green line is selected as the sung lead; the lower chord/arpeggio voices and the instrumental Intro chapter are omitted. Pitch classes were read from the labelled piano roll; rhythms are an ear/visual reduction quantized to eighth/quarter beats at the retained 130 BPM, not a claim of an exact original-recording or engraved-score transcription. The two title calls each continue into the distinct descending answer and vocal closing line. Most tutorial vocal notes C#5-F#5 and A4-B4 are reduced two octaves to C#3-F#3 and A2-B2; the brief E4 pickup before the first closing rise is octave-folded to E3 so it stays above the bass. Instrumental turnarounds are shortened to two beats between halves. The last A2 at beat54 is an arranger-added tonic cadence, after the sustained B2 vocal ending, not an additional original sung note. Official composer/publisher listing confirms Per Gessle and A major; official lyric structure is used only to identify the vocal phrase order, with no recorded voice or lyric audio sampled. Chords, rhythm section, responses and exact compact edit are creative accompaniment choices.
musical_direction: The FART VOICE SINGS the refrain from the first beat: clear low A2-F#3 lead, no instrumental intro or riff loop. Keep the lead well in front, with simple quiet root/fifth bass, compact backbeat and restrained chord stabs. Leave the long sung notes audible and distinct; do not answer over their attacks. Build the second vocal half a little, then hold its different closing note and finish with a short low A-major ensemble cadence. All audio remains made from the nine recorded fart sources.

musical_direction: Tight trance at exactly 140 BPM. Preserve all 56 corrected notes per 16-beat riff, repeated three times, with the accepted B3-E4-D4-A3 register. The sixteenth-note lead is the main attraction: crisp alternating Blota/Snabbisen attacks, a stable pitched body, no timing jitter and gates at most 0.12 seconds or 67% of the written duration. Keep the tatatatata separation audible. Add a low four-on-the-floor fart kick, offbeat bass pulses, short airy squeaks and thin backbeat splats; harmonic stabs stay sparse and quiet. Grow from a lean first pass to extra percussion and occasional muted bubbles in pass three. Avoid long wet tails, busy fills during dense lead runs, or any octave or tempo change.

title: Ring of Fire
source_notes: Upper trumpet line in the Gary Badger transcription, with source written F#5-G#5-E5-F#5 and D#5-E5-C#5-D#5 moved to D4-E4-C4-D4 and B3-C4-A3-B3 for the solo fart instrument. All 32 melody pitches, onsets, durations and the existing fixed source transposition are preserved exactly from the previously accepted score, as are all chord-event beats, pitches and durations. musical_direction: Playful lively country/mariachi fart band at 144 BPM, increased from the previously approved 114 BPM for a faster live-style feel, with the same 32 lead notes in D4-E4-C4-D4 and B3-C4-A3-B3 register. Keep the paired half-beat trumpet-hook snaps and all long phrase notes intact. Use alternating low root/fifth farts on the boom beats and short nasal chord puffs on the chick beats; soft ticking farts and occasional dry splats carry the train rhythm. Add gentle low brass-like doubling on long notes, tiny question-and-answer splutters after phrase anchors, and a more colorful second 20-beat pass. Preserve the 20-beat hook and its short turnaround, with no new intro and no changes to the melody event rhythm.

title: The Final Countdown
source_notes: Pitches, exact sixteenth/eighth-note rhythm and ties visually checked against the piano melody on printed pages 1-4 of arranger Pierre Loiselle's self-published score. Uses its bars 1-8, then 13-16, with an added F# minor cadence. Lead uses original-key pitches C#5/B4/F#4/D5 etc. Tied notes are merged. The initial 1.5 beats of rest are omitted so the recognisable C#5-B4-C#5 fanfare starts instantly. Tempo 118 BPM and octave choices are arrangement decisions; this is an independently sequenced fart arrangement, not original-recording audio. Harmonic extensions are optional accompaniment colour. For version 5.0 the complete melody and all harmonies are transposed down five semitones from the accepted F# minor score into C# minor. Rhythm, note durations and tempo are unchanged.
musical_direction: Arena-rock fart fanfare in a lower C# minor register. Keep the accepted melody, phrasing, bass gallop and orchestration, transposing every pitched voice down five semitones.

title: The Imperial March
source_notes: Melody and note durations visually checked against the official Faber/Warner-Chappell piano sample, printed page 28, bars 5-16 (the 4-bar introduction is omitted). The publisher sample is marked approximately 100 BPM; 108 BPM is the creative arrangement tempo. All melody pitches are transposed down one octave from that piano notation. The defining figures use dotted eighth + sixteenth (0.75 + 0.25 quarter-note beats), not straight eighths or triplets. F# and Eb in the upper chromatic descent are enharmonic spellings of the printed F# and D#. Chord events below are simplified arrangement guidance, not a transcription of the original orchestration.
musical_direction: A grand, silly fart brass band, 26.67 seconds before the release tail. Start the recognizable lead at beat 0 without an intro. Opening register G3, climactic high G4. Keep melody pitches exact; make rests and the dotted-eighth/sixteenth snaps crisp, with note gates around 75-85% except the final half-note. Alternate several pitched short dry rasps and resonant brass-like farts across melodic notes without changing the fundamental. Layer a quieter octave-down bass fart on strong beats, sparse triad stabs (two or three different timbres) under the first three repeated notes, and airy little puffs as snare on beats 1 and 3 of each bar. Add restrained marching 16th puffs in the written rests at beats 15, 21.0-21.5, 25.0-25.5, 37.0-37.5 and 41.0-41.5; avoid masking the Eb/Bb lead snaps. Give bars 9-12 a larger supporting ensemble and a small fill into beat 44. Finish with the G minor cadence and one low, rounded fart release. Lower harmonies are a pad/stab layer, never a competing tune.

title: Seven Nation Army
source_notes: Riff pitches and durations visually verified against online-skills own educational bass notation, published on the Polish government ZPE portal (CC BY 3.0). Its Riff I supplies E E G E D / C B at onsets 0,1.5,2,2.75,3.5 / 4,6. Riff III supplies C D C B at 4,4.75,5.5,6. Riff II is eight G eighths then eight A eighths. The displayed bass octave is used as the fart-lead register (E3 opening); it is an arrangement choice rather than the recording sounding register. The source text mislabels the tonal centre C major; the notation supports E minor. Tempo 124 BPM, section order, all accompaniment voicings and the last E3 cadence are independent arrangement decisions. No original-recording audio is used.
musical_direction: 27.1 seconds before a short release tail. Begin immediately with the iconic riff, with a firm and very clear E3 lead; keep every riff in the same register and timbre family so the listener can follow it. The bass-root G2/A2 turnaround intentionally sits below the E3 riff. Use one tight woody/rasping pitched fart as the main voice and another rounder one as occasional accents, with stable pitch bodies and approximately 82-90 percent note gates. The dotted rhythm must stay exact; do not quantise the .75-beat notes into straight eighths. First two bars: expose riff with only soft low kick farts on beats 0 and 2. Bars 3-4: add dry papery snare/clap farts on beats 1 and 3 and a restrained eighth-note breath/hiss pulse. Bars 5-6: the G/A eighth-note power-chord build grows into the next riff, with a tiny snare-fart fill in the last beat. Bars 7-10: fuller stadium-size response, quiet octave-down bass tracking the root movement, broad fifth stabs and a little stereo rasp. Prefer eight or nine recorded fart colours across percussion/fills, but keep the melodic lead dominant and do not alternate random samples on every riff note. Bars 11-12: stronger G/A rise, short puffs becoming a sixteenth-note fill at beat 47. Bars 13-14: final full riff, then C-D-C-B and an added E3 at beat 55. Land all voices with the final E chord; one low rounded release, no additional busy solo. Harmony entries are newly arranged root/fifth/octave voicings, not a competing counter-melody. Keep bass quieter than the riff, kick and snare distinct, and short lead notes clean enough to identify the hook.

title: Through the Fire and Flames
composer: Herman Li, ZP Theart, Sam Totman and Vadim Pruzhanov
source_notes: Short-intro edit of the verified 30-second arrangement: retain old beats 0-8 at output 0-8, move the connecting run from old 60-64 to output 8-12, move the complete electric hook from old 64-96 to output 12-44, and move the arranged closing cadence from old 96-100 to output 44-48. Total 12 bars / 48 quarter-note beats / 14.4 seconds at 200 BPM. Original key C minor, 4/4, 200 BPM (licensed Musicnotes lists 199; Hal Leonard artist-approved preview marks 200). Straight sixteenths remain 0.25 beat = 75 ms. Output bars 1-2 (beats 0-8) retain the licensed Hal Leonard page-1 Guitar 3 two-bar top-voice reduction once, all 32 exact sounding guitar notes. This is an intentional melodic reduction of simultaneous acoustic voices; no single community MIDI track is claimed to equal the licensed reduction. The higher moving eighth-note pitches agree independently with the maximum of the 12-track Acoustic+Keyboard and Acoustic Guitar parts; the licensed reduction supplies the explicit C4 interleaved pedal. Output bar 3 (beats 8-12) retains the exact 16-event Acoustic+Keyboard connecting run from original bar 16, source beats 60-64 / ticks 28800-30720, Songparts dPOfCHp4g18SSKCN, 480 ticks per beat. Output bars 4-11 (beats 12-44) retain all 123 exact onsets, pitches and durations of Lead 1 from original source bars 17-24 / beats 64-96 / ticks 30720-46080, with the existing fixed -12-semitone electric-section register change. Optional harmony retains the same 123 Lead 2 events and the same -12-semitone register change. All retained melody and harmony durations are unchanged; only their onsets are shifted. The two alternate 12-track transcriptions corroborate the intro and electric hook structure. The 14-track lKrvLtRPuj0rrCfY version was rejected because of implausible acoustic D3 pedal glitches and discordant electric-hook pitches. Output beat 44 C4/Eb4 held for four beats and the final C-minor chord are the existing newly arranged resolution, moved intact from old beat 96. The first C-minor chord is trimmed from 16 to 8 beats; the retained final four beats of the old G-major chord become output 8-12. Remaining kept chord pitches and durations are unchanged. Chords are simplified guidance derived from source bass/harmony, not a transcription of every original rhythm-guitar attack. No original-song recordings are included.
musical_direction: 14.4-second score with a short recognizable acoustic arpeggio: play the first two bars for 2.4 seconds, immediately play the original connecting run for 1.2 seconds, then hit the complete eight-bar twin-guitar power-metal hook at output beat 12 / 3.6 seconds. Preserve every retained pitch and the exact 75 ms lead onset grid. Make the sampled fart character unmistakable and much stronger: prominent unfiltered natural fart attacks, audible rasp, burbles, rough lower-octave doubling and contrasting sample textures around a clear pitched core. Keep enough separation to hear every sixteenth. Let several different fart samples answer one another, with natural fart replies every four beats and at phrase boundaries; preserve the actual melody instead of randomizing its notes. Restrained harmony only during the electric hook, with low chugging power chords, double-kick fart pulses and concise snare puffs. Keep the lead above bass and drums. Retain the final original hook run and hold the existing C-minor closing cadence for output beats 44-48, followed by a longer resonant natural fart tail. No joke failure, speed collapse, random pitch scrambling or slowing down at the end.
